deep.reconstruction:
This page is a draft of Riemann's 1851 Inaugural Dissertation ('Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'). It has two unrelated blocks. The upper block is the regularity argument (Dissertation §§10–11). The lower block is an inserted digression on the connectivity of surfaces (Dissertation §6).

(A) Regularity of harmonic functions via Green's representation.
- Setting (from the preceding text in the Dissertation): u is a real function on the surface T satisfying Δu = 0. O_0 = (x_0, y_0) is an interior point, r is the distance from O_0 to the boundary point (x, y), and p is the inward normal along the boundary ∂T.
- Green's theorem then gives (the constant is my supplement, not visible on the page): u(x_0,y_0) = (1/(2π)) ∮_{∂T} ( log r · ∂u/∂p − u · ∂(log r)/∂p ) ds.
- Riemann now treats O_0 as moving. In the integrand only log r, ∂log r/∂x and ∂log r/∂y depend on (x_0, y_0); the boundary data u and ∂u/∂p do not.
- For each boundary element, as long as O_0 stays in the interior of T, these quantities and all their derivatives in x_0, y_0 are continuous and finite. The reason given is that the derivatives are rational functions with only powers of r in the denominator, and r is bounded away from 0. For example, ∂/∂x_0 log r = −(x − x_0)/r², and ∂/∂p log r = ((x − x_0) cos(p,x) + (y − y_0) cos(p,y))/r².
- Differentiating under the integral sign, the same holds for u_0 = u(O_0) and all its derivatives. So u is C^∞ (indeed real-analytic) in the interior.
- The garbled final lines say that arbitrary assumptions about u or its derivatives at isolated points are excluded. The function is determined by its boundary values, so isolated-point irregularities are impossible; this is the germ of the removable-singularity remarks in the Dissertation.

(B) Order of connectivity (Ordnung des Zusammenhangs).
- The definition sits on the missing preceding text: a number attached to a surface, essentially the number of cross-cuts needed to reduce the surface to simply connected pieces, minus the number of pieces. Riemann proposes to call it the order of connectivity and lists how it behaves under four kinds of cuts.
- Querschnitt (cross-cut: a non-self-intersecting arc from boundary to boundary): the order decreases by 1. This holds by definition.
- Rückschnitt (arc from a boundary point to an interior point, without self-intersection): no change. Reason: extending it by a further Querschnitt from its interior endpoint to the boundary turns the whole into a single Querschnitt. Then total = −1 and continuation = −1, so the Rückschnitt contributes 0.
- Innerer Schnitt (arc joining two interior points): the order increases by 1. Reason: a Querschnitt from the boundary to a point of the slit (the slit is now boundary) gives −1, and the union is a tree attached to the boundary, i.e. Rückschnitte, total 0. Hence the inner cut contributes +1.
- Closed simple interior curve: no change. Reason: it is composed of an inner cut (+1) and a Querschnitt (−1) joining the endpoints along the rest of the curve.
- Final sentence (only partly legible): the order of a surface consisting of several pieces is expressed through the orders of its pieces. In the Dissertation's normalisation it is additive.
- The next page specialises to one-piece surfaces. There 'n-fach zusammenhängend' means reducible to simply connected by n−1 cross-cuts, and the boundary-component parity results follow.

Modern restatement of (B): for a compact bordered surface, connectivity = 1 − χ, i.e. the first Betti number for a connected surface.
- A cross-cut lowers b_1 by 1.
- A slit from the boundary leaves χ unchanged, since it is a deformation retract.
- An interior slit removes a 'disk', so χ drops by 1.
- Cutting along a closed curve leaves χ unchanged because χ(S¹) = 0.
errors: No mathematical errors. All four connectivity rules are correct under Riemann's additive normalisation (order = cuts − pieces, or equivalently 1 − χ summed over pieces).
The Green-formula block is heavily corrected and the written text omits the constant 1/(2π) and the explicit statement Δu = 0. These are supplied from the Dissertation, not from the page.

Differentiation under the integral sign is asserted without justification. It is legitimate here because the integrand is smooth in (x_0, y_0) uniformly on the compact boundary while O_0 stays at positive distance from it.

The justification for the inner-cut rule ('dieser zerfällt durch einen Querschnitt in einen Rückschnitt') is compressed. It needs the observation that a cut from the boundary to a point of the slit is a Querschnitt, because the slit is now part of the boundary.

results.what: Harmonic functions are infinitely differentiable in the interior, deduced from the Green representation formula with log r kernel (derivatives in the pole are rational in r).
results.modern_name: Interior regularity / smoothness of harmonic functions via Green's representation formula
results.usually_credited_to: Green (1828), Gauss (1840); standard in potential theory

results.what: Behaviour of the order of connectivity under cross-cuts (−1), boundary slits (0), interior slits (+1) and closed interior curves (0).
results.modern_name: Connectivity number / first Betti number, 1 − Euler characteristic, of bordered surfaces under cutting

results.what: Additivity of the order of connectivity over the components of a surface consisting of several pieces.
results.modern_name: Additivity of Euler characteristic over components

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of passages that appear in Riemann's published 1851 Dissertation (the regularity argument of §§10–11 and the connectivity discussion of §6). The content is well known and already attributed to him.

checkable.sympy: x,y,x0,y0=symbols('x y x0 y0',real=True); r=sqrt((x-x0)**2+(y-y0)**2); simplify(diff(log(r),x0)+(x-x0)/r**2)==0
checkable.asserts: ∂/∂x_0 log r = −(x−x_0)/r², a rational function with a power of r in the denominator
log r is harmonic away from O_0 (the kernel of Green's formula)
Higher derivatives of log r in the pole are rational with only powers of r in the denominator
An interior slit raises connectivity 1−χ by 1 (the disk becomes an annulus-type surface)
A cross-cut (removing an arc meeting the boundary at its ends) raises χ by 1 and so lowers connectivity by 1, e.g. annulus to disk

transcription_corrections: Line 2: the deleted '[-und dlog r/dp-]' is a deleted 'und' plus a struck fraction; the retained list is 'log r, dlog r/dx, dlog r/dy'.
'nach dem selben gilt dasselbe auch für die Function u_0 und ihre Diff.quot.': the word read as 'dem-selben' is more likely 'demselben' / 'derselben' (by the same argument).

Last lines of the top block likely read approximately: '...ihre Diff.quot.; [es sind] daher Annahmen, die einen Ausdruck einer selbständigen Unstetigkeit bei den Diff.quot. ganz willkürliche Annahmen in einzelnen Punkten gestatten würden, ausgeschlossen'. Uncertain.
'Rückschnitt' definition: 'einen von einem Begrenzungspunkte, ohne sich zu schneiden, nach einem innern Punkte gehende Linie' is consistent with the image.

'denn dieser ... zerfällt durch einen Querschnitt in einen Rückschnitt': the image shows 'denn dieser [struck] durch einen Querschnitt in einen Rückschnitt übergeht', i.e. 'übergeht' rather than 'zerfällt'.
'weil diese durch Ueberg. einen inneren Schnitt': more likely 'weil diese als Ueberg[ang]' / 'durch Verbindung eines inneren Schnittes und eines Querschnitts gebildet werden kann'. Uncertain.

Final sentence: probably 'Ferner wird die Ordnung des Zusammenhangs einer aus mehreren Stücken bestehenden Fläche = der Summe der Ordnungen der Zusammenhänge dieser Stücke ...'. The transcription's 'wie sich ... verhält' is doubtful.
